nodes.name: Co-reduction synthesis
nodes.procedure: The NA-Ru₃Ni was synthesized by the co-reduction of ruthenium acetylacetonate (Ru(acac)₃) and nickle acetylacetonate (Ni(acac)₂) in a mixed solution containing benzyl alcohol and resorcinol at 180°C for 1 h.
nodes.source_text: Typically, the NA-Ru₃Ni was synthesized by the co-reduction of ruthenium acetylacetonate (Ru(acac)₃) and nickle acetylacetonate (Ni(acac)₂) in a mixed solution containing benzyl alcohol and resorcinol at 180°C for 1 h (see Methods for details, Fig. S1, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM evidences formation of nanocone-assembled structure with high purity and uniformity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The representative transmission electron microscopy (TEM) ... images evidence the formation of nanocone-assembled structure with high purity and uniformity (Fig. 1a,b, and Fig. S2, ESI†).

properties.description: Transmission Electron Microscopy image showing nanostructure

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows average curvature radius of cone tip around 1.3 nm and atomic-resolution image confirms HCP structure with periodic ABAB stacking mode along [010] zone axis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The assembled structure has an average size of 36.2 nm (Fig. S2b, ESI†) and the average curvature radius of cone tip is around 1.3 nm (Fig. 1c,d and Fig. S3, ESI†). The atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM image recorded along the [010] zone axis clearly shows the periodic ABAB stacking mode, corroborating the hexagonal close-packed (HCP) structure (Fig. 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS line-scanning and elemental mapping show homogeneous distribution of Ru and Ni throughout the structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) line-scanning profiles (Fig. 1f) and elemental mapping (Fig. 1g) indicate a homogenous distribution of Ru and Ni through the whole structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS confirms atomic ratio of Ru:Ni ≈ 3.0:1.0.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic ratio of Ru:Ni was further estimated to be about 3.0:1.0 according to the inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS, Fig. 1h) and STEM-EDS (Fig. S4, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey verifies coexistence of Ru and Ni; surface atomic ratio matches ICP-MS and STEM-EDS; high-resolution Ru 3p and Ni 2p spectra indicate metallic states with Ru 3p peak negatively shifted by 0.32 eV relative to commercial Ru/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) survey spectrum verifies the coexistence of Ru and Ni element (Fig. S5, ESI†). The surface atomic ratio of Ru:Ni obtained from the XPS is in line with that from the ICP-MS and STEM-EDS. As shown in Fig. 1i, the high-resolution Ru 3p and Ni 2p spectra indicate that most of the surface Ru and Ni are in metallic state. Notably, the binding energy of Ru 3p peak for the as-synthesized Ru₃Ni is negatively shifted by 0.32 eV relative to that of commercial Ru/C

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms identical phase structure across NA-Ru₃Ni and annealed samples with no peak shifts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction analysis indicates the identical phase structure and composition of the samples, as evidenced by the absence of the shifts in the diffraction peaks (Fig. S17, ESI†).
